elements.element: Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it
elements.evidence: "Customer shall own all deliverables and all work product created for Customer under this Agreement or any Exhibit"

elements.element: Vendor assigns deliverables/work product to Customer
elements.evidence: "Kubient hereby assigns all such deliverables and all such work product to Customer"
"Kubient retains all right, title and interest in and to its pre-existing intellectual property, including the Auction Platform"

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: "grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor intellectual property embedded in the deliverables"

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: "Customer owns and retains all right, title and interest, including all intellectual property rights, in and to the Content, the Properties and all other data provided by, or collected on behalf of, Customer"
"Nothing in this Agreement creates any joint ownership of intellectual property."

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: insertion addresses only "pre-existing intellectual property, including the Auction Platform"; no generic tools/know-how language

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables
elements.evidence: licence is limited to "any Vendor intellectual property embedded in the deliverables" with no worldwide, modify or sublicense rights

reasons: All six atomic preferred elements are present in a single concise inserted clause: Customer ownership plus express assignment of deliverables and work product, Vendor retention of pre-existing IP, the perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free embedded-Vendor-IP licence, Customer Data rights, and an express no-joint-ownership statement.

The insertion correctly adds no fallback-only rights (worldwide, modify, sublicense), so the two levels are not mixed; fallback is independently unmet, which is immaterial given the locked preferred target.

Minimal: the Agreement had no ownership provision at all, and a short standalone clause is the least intrusive fix; no untouched sentence was rewritten and the compliance, disclaimer and trademark/publicity terms remain effective.

Minor drafting note only (not a deviation): the inserted section is numbered "14." while an existing "14. General Provisions" follows, and the parenthetical "Kubient (Vendor)" introduces "Vendor" as an ad hoc label; renumbering to 14/15 and using "Kubient" consistently would tidy this without changing substance.
